extraReferences.title: Argyropelecus aculeatus
extraReferences.publisher: Fishes of Texas (University of Texas at Austin), species account after McEachran & Fechhelm

anatomy.lede: Seen side-on it is a deep, flattened blade of silver, edged below with rows of light organs.

hotspots.label: Eye
hotspots.text: A light organ aimed at the eye shines into it through a dip in the iris, possibly so the fish can compare its own glow with daylight from above.

hotspots.label: Jaws
hotspots.text: The jaws are large, with long, backward-curving teeth and two enlarged canines in the lower jaw.

hotspots.label: Dorsal spine and fin
hotspots.text: A tall spine stands in front of the dorsal fin, which has 9 soft rays.

hotspots.label: Silver flank
hotspots.text: The mirror-like sides, with diffuse dark pigment on the trunk, help it blend into the dim light filtering down through the twilight zone.

hotspots.label: Belly light organs
hotspots.text: Rows of photophores along the belly give off a pale blue light, in a pattern particular to each species.

hotspots.label: Tail light organs
hotspots.text: A separate cluster of photophores sits under the tail, with spines below and in front of them and dark pigment concentrated above.

senses.lede: Its eyes do two jobs: looking up for food and, it seems, checking its own disguise.

senses.name: Sharp eyes for the twilight
senses.text: Measurements of its lens optics suggest it can resolve details about 0.08 degrees apart.

senses.name: A built-in light meter
senses.text: Light from the eye-facing photophore passes through clear tissue, the iris dip and the lens, and probably lands as an unfocused spot on an accessory retina. This may let the fish set its belly lights to match the light it sees above.

body.lede: Its camouflage depends on light organs that are carefully shielded, positioned and timed to develop.

systems.title: A shielded reference light
systems.text: The eye-facing photophore is wrapped on its front and outer sides by a layer of melanin, so its light goes into the eye instead of out into the water where it could give the fish away.

systems.title: Found wherever counter-shading lights exist
systems.text: Across three families of related fishes, every species with belly lights capable of counter-illumination had an eye-facing photophore. Two species that cannot counter-illuminate lacked one.

systems.title: A spiny keel
systems.text: Well-developed spines sit on the rear of the belly, the hind one much larger, and the keel there juts below the line of the body.

survival.lede: It hides by day and feeds by night, using light, silver and timing.

tactics.title: Erasing its shadow
tactics.text: The belly lights match the colour and brightness of daylight from above, hiding its silhouette from midwater hunters looking up.

tactics.title: Feeding at dusk
tactics.text: It rises towards the surface early at night and is a selective feeder, mainly on tiny shelled crustaceans called conchoecid ostracods, with some copepods and larval crabs, shrimps and fishes.

tactics.title: Quick to recover
tactics.text: FishBase rates its resilience as high, with a population thought able to double in less than 15 months, though this estimate is preliminary.

life.lede: A short life, lived between the twilight zone by day and shallower water at night.

stages.name: Egg
stages.text: Fertilisation is external. Eggs are scattered in open water and the parents give no care.

stages.name: Young fish
stages.text: The adult pattern of light organs develops at about 15 mm in length.

stages.name: Juvenile
stages.text: Young fish have a clear, unpigmented bar just in front of the tail stalk.

stages.name: Adult
stages.text: Sexes are separate. Females spawn in repeated batches, and half are mature by about 39 mm in standard length.
